statements.statement: Paper A presents a method where a convolutional neural network (CNN) learns the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile.
Paper A's method generates steering commands from a single front-facing center camera.
Paper B introduces ChauffeurNet, a recurrent neural network (RNN) that takes mid-level input and outputs driving trajectories for control.
ChauffeurNet incorporates components such as FeatureNet and AgentRNN.
ChauffeurNet uses a memory model with recurrent feedback between iterations.
Both methods rely on different input representations and network architectures to produce control outputs for autonomous driving.

parsed.type_evidence: Claims 1, 2 (CNN, end-to-end, camera input); Claims 3, 4, 5 (RNN, mid-level input, recurrent feedback, FeatureNet/AgentRNN); both describe methods for producing control outputs.
